Rashi on Pesachim 93a:10:1.hebrew: תשלומין דראשון - ומאן דלא איחזי בראשון לא מיחייב אשני. ומיהו, תקוני לראשון מכרת — אם הזיד בראשון — לא מתקן ליה. הלכך, חייב כרת על הראשון ואפילו עשה את השני, ופטור על השני אם שגג בראשון והזיד בשני, דהא לית ליה חיובא באנפי נפשיה, ובראשון הרי שגג:
Rashi on Pesachim 93a:10:1.english: A compensation for the first - And one who was not fit [to offer it] on the first [Pesach] is not obligated on the second. However, [as for] repairing the first from [the penalty of] karet — if he acted intentionally on the first — it does not repair it. Therefore, he is liable to karet for the first even if he observed the second, and he is exempt for the second if he acted unwittingly on the first and intentionally on the second, for [the second] has no obligation in its own right, and on the first he acted unwittingly.

Rashi on Pesachim 93a:11:1.hebrew: תקנתא דראשון - מכרת דיליה, דאפילו הזיד בראשון, השני פוטרו מן הכרת:
Rashi on Pesachim 93a:11:1.english: A remedy for the first - From its karet, for even if one acted intentionally on the first [Pesach], the second [Pesach] exempts him from the karet.

Rashi on Pesachim 93a:12:1.hebrew: אי נמי קרבן ה' לא הקריב וגו' - ד"כי" משמש בארבע לשונות, וזה בלשון "אי" דרשינן ליה, ולא קאי אדלעיל מיניה לפרושי טעמא למילתא קמייתא כמו לשון "דהא", אלא מילתא אחריתי היא, כמו: "כי יקרא" (דברים כב), "כי תכלה לעשר" (שם כו), "כי תפגע" (שמות כג):
Rashi on Pesachim 93a:12:1.english: If also he did not bring the offering of the Lord, etc. - For [the word] ki [in the verse] is used in four senses, and this [occurrence] we expound in the sense of i ["if"]; and it does not refer back to what precedes it to explain the reason for the first matter, like the sense of deha ["because"], rather it is a separate matter, like: "If [a bird's nest] chance" (Deuteronomy 22), "If you finish tithing" (ibid. 26), "If you encounter" (Exodus 23).

Rashi on Pesachim 93a:1:1.hebrew: מה טמא שיש ספק בידו לעשות - אי לאו דדחייה רחמנא, דהא קמן קאי:
Rashi on Pesachim 93a:1:1.english: Just as one who is ritually impure, who has the means to do [it] - if not that the Merciful One deferred him, for behold, he is standing before us.

Rashi on Pesachim 93a:1:2.english: And does not do [so] - For the Merciful One forbade him from doing [so].

Rashi on Pesachim 93a:1:3.hebrew: אף דרך רחוקה שספק בידו לעשות - שהיה לו שלוחים לשלח, וקאמר רחמנא דאינו עושה, דמדחה דחייה:
Rashi on Pesachim 93a:1:3.english: So too, [one on] a distant journey who has the means to do [so] - For he had agents to send, yet the Merciful One says that he does not do [so], for he is deferred.

Rashi on Pesachim 93a:2:1.hebrew: ר"ע סבר אין שוחטין וזורקין על טמא שרץ - ואע"ג דחזי לאורתא. והאי ספק דקאמר, ה"ק: מה טמא שספק בידו לעשות, דחזי למיכל לאורתא, ואפילו הכי אין שוחטין וזורקין עליו; ואנן ס"ל שוחטין וזורקין, הלכך האי נמי דיכול ליכנס בשעת אכילה שוחטין וזורקין עליו:
Rashi on Pesachim 93a:2:1.english: Rabbi Akiva holds [that] one may not slaughter and sprinkle [the blood] on behalf of one who is impure [from] a creeping animal - even though he is fit [to eat it] in the evening. And this [phrase] "has the means" that [the Gemara] said, this is what it means: Just as an impure person who has the means in his hand to perform [the offering] — for he is fit to eat [it] in the evening — and even so, one may not slaughter and sprinkle on his behalf; but we hold [that] one may slaughter and sprinkle [on his behalf], therefore [for] this one as well, who is able to enter [Jerusalem] by the time of eating, one may slaughter and sprinkle on his behalf.

Rashi on Pesachim 93a:3:1.english: And those who had sexual relations with menstruating women - For all of these [involve] prolonged impurity.

Rashi on Pesachim 93a:3:2.english: And one who was ritually impure - [Ritually impure] from a corpse.

Rashi on Pesachim 93a:4:1.hebrew: וא"כ - דאף אלו עושים את השני:
Rashi on Pesachim 93a:4:1.english: And if so - That even these observe the second [Pesach].

Rashi on Pesachim 93a:4:2.english: Why is "ritually impure" stated - [This is said] in astonishment.

Rashi on Pesachim 93a:4:3.hebrew: אלא למה נאמר דרך רחוקה - אי משום דאי בעי למיעבד לא תעביד, הא בדרך רחוקה הוא! וא"ת שלא ישלח פסחו, וכדרב ששת — האי תנא לית ליה, אלא כרב נחמן סבירא ליה דאמר הורצה; דאי כרב ששת, איצטריך דרך רחוקה למימר דאי בעי לא ליעביד:
Rashi on Pesachim 93a:4:3.english: Rather, why is "a distant journey" stated - If [you say it is] because if he wants to perform [it], do not perform [it] — behold, he is on a distant journey! And if you say [it teaches] that he should not send his Paschal lamb [with a messenger], in accordance with Rav Sheshet — this Tanna does not hold [that]; rather, he holds like Rav Nachman, who said it was accepted; for if [he held] like Rav Sheshet, "a distant journey" would be needed to state that if he wants [to send it], he may not do [so].

Rashi on Pesachim 93a:5:1.english: Is [she] obligated - For [the baraita] taught menstruating women and women who have given birth.

Rashi on Pesachim 93a:5:2.english: I might [have thought] they would not [observe], etc. - And [the baraita] does not teach zavot [women with an abnormal discharge] and women who have given birth.

Rashi on Pesachim 93a:6:1.hebrew: הא רבי יוסי - דאמר בפירקין דלעיל (פסחים דף צא:), נשים בשני שוחטין עליהן בפני עצמן:
Rashi on Pesachim 93a:6:1.english: This [is] Rabbi Yosei - Who said in our chapter above (Pesachim 91b): Women on the second [Pesach], one slaughters for them by themselves.

Rashi on Pesachim 93a:6:2.hebrew: הא ר"י ור"ש - דאמרי רשות:
Rashi on Pesachim 93a:6:2.english: This [baraita is] Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Shimon - Who say [it is] optional.

Rashi on Pesachim 93a:7:1.hebrew: חייב כרת על הראשון וחייב כרת על השני - חיוב כרת יש על זה ועל זה, ובחד גברא לא משכחת לה, דתרי קטלי בחד גברא ליכא. ואם לענין דאם שגג בשניהן יתחייב שתי חטאות — ליכא למימר הכי, דכרת דפסח אין חייבין על שגגתו חטאת, דתנן בכריתות (דף ב.): הפסח והמילה מצות עשה היא, ואין חטאת באה אלא על שגגת כרת של לאו, דכתיב (ויקרא ד) אשר לא תעשינה. אלא נפקא מינה דאם שגג בא' מהן והזיד בחבירו — חייב; אי נמי, לגר שנתגייר בין שני פסחים:
Rashi on Pesachim 93a:7:1.english: He is liable to karet for the first and liable to karet for the second - There is liability to karet for this [first Pesach] and for that [second Pesach]. However, in one person you do not find [both applying], for there are not two [karet penalties] in one person. And if [you suggest it is relevant] with respect to [the case] where if he transgressed both unwittingly he would be liable for two sin-offerings — one cannot say so, because for the karet of Pesach one is not liable for a sin-offering upon its unwitting transgression, as we learned in a Mishnah in Keritot (2a): "The Pesach-offering and circumcision are positive commandments, and a sin-offering is brought only for the unwitting transgression of a karet-bearing negative commandment, as it is written (Leviticus 4[:2]): 'which should not be done.'" Rather, the practical difference is that if he erred unwittingly in one of them and acted intentionally in the other, he is liable; alternatively, [it applies] to a convert who converted between the two Pesachs.

Rashi on Pesachim 93a:7:2.hebrew: ופטור על השני - ואם שגג בראשון והזיד בשני, פטור:
Rashi on Pesachim 93a:7:2.english: And [one is] exempt for the second - And if he acted unwittingly regarding the first [Pesach] and intentionally regarding the second, he is exempt [from karet].

Rashi on Pesachim 93a:7:3.hebrew: אף על הראשון - אם הזיד, אינו חייב כרת עד שיזיד אף בשני; אבל אם עשה את השני או שגג בו, פטור לגמרי, דשני תשלומים דראשון ותקנתא דראשון הוא, ומזיד שלו הוא גמרו של כרת דראשון. הלכך, באיזה מהן ששגג, פטור:
Rashi on Pesachim 93a:7:3.english: Even for the first - If he acted intentionally [regarding the first], he is not liable to karet unless he also acts intentionally regarding the second; but if he observed the second [Pesach] or acted unwittingly regarding it, he is completely exempt, for the second is a makeup for the first and a remedy for the first, and intentional [neglect] of it is the completion of the karet for the first. Therefore, whichever of them he acted unwittingly in, he is exempt.

Rashi on Pesachim 93a:8:1.english: And they follow their reasoning - Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi] and Rabbi Natan.

Rashi on Pesachim 93a:8:2.english: Who grew up - [Pubic] hairs grew on him.

Rashi on Pesachim 93a:8:3.hebrew: חייבין לעשות את השני - דקסבר רגל בפני עצמו הוא, ואית ליה חיובא באנפי נפשיה, ואפי' למאן דלא איחזי בראשון:
Rashi on Pesachim 93a:8:3.english: [They are] obligated to observe the second [Pesach] - For he [Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi] holds [that it] is an independent festival, and it has an obligation of its own, even for one who was not eligible on the first [Pesach].

Tosafot on Pesachim 93a:1:1.hebrew: ה"ג בכל הספרים, וכן גרסינן בספרי (פר' בהעלותך): "מה טמא שאין ספק בידו כו'". ומיתני התם אפלוגתא דר"א ור"ע, ומייתי ר"ע ראיה לדבריו: מה טמא שאין ספק בידו לעשות מפני טומאה, אף דרך רחוקה שאין ספק בידו לעשות — שרחוק כ"כ שאין יכול לבא בשעת שחיטה לעולא, או בשעת אכילה לרב יהודה. ומייתי לה רב ששת: מדקאמר "ואינו עושה", משמע דלא הורצה, דלכל מילי יליף דרך רחוקה מטמא. ומשני רב נחמן דר"ע סבר אין שוחטין וזורקין, ולכך יליף דרך רחוקה מטמא, דתרוייהו חזו בשעת אכילה ולא חזו בשעת שחיטה, ולדידיה נמי אם זרק לא הורצה; אבל אנא סבירא לי שוחטין וזורקין, והשתא ליכא למילף דלא הורצה בדרך רחוקה כמו בטמא מת, דשאני טמא מת דלא חזי בשעת אכילה. ורב ששת סבר נמי שוחטין, דאין סברא שיחלוקו בזה, אלא דסברי דר"ע גמר מטמא מת אע"ג דלא דמי ליה כ"כ. ונראה לר"י דלאו מהיקשא יליף דרך רחוקה מטמא, אלא במה מצינו; דאי מהיקשא, מאי קא משני רב נחמן דסבר שוחטין? מ"מ ניגמר מיניה, דאין משיבין על ההיקש! וק"ק לר"י, דאי לאו היקשא הוא, איכא טובא למיפרך:
Tosafot on Pesachim 93a:1:1.english: This is the reading in all the manuscripts, and so we read in the Sifrei (Parashat Beha'alotecha): "Just as one who is ritually impure, who has no ability to observe [the Pesaḥ offering], etc." And it is taught there regarding the dispute between Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Akiva, and Rabbi Akiva brings a proof for his view: "Just as one who is ritually impure, who has no ability to observe [it] because of ritual impurity, so too one on a distant journey, who has no ability to observe [it]" — for he is so far away that he cannot arrive by the time of slaughter according to Ulla, or by the time of eating according to Rav Yehudah. And Rav Sheshet brings it [as a proof]: since it states "and he does not observe [it]," it implies that [if someone slaughtered and sprinkled on his behalf] it is not accepted, for in all respects he derives "distant journey" from "ritually impure." And Rav Naḥman answers that Rabbi Akiva holds that one may not slaughter and sprinkle [the blood on behalf of one impure from a creeping creature], and therefore he derives "distant journey" from "ritually impure," since both are fit at the time of eating yet are not fit at the time of slaughter, and according to him as well, if one did sprinkle [the blood], it is not accepted; "but I hold that one may slaughter and sprinkle, and now one cannot derive that it is not accepted for one on a distant journey just as for one impure from a corpse, because one impure from a corpse is different, as he is not fit at the time of eating." And Rav Sheshet also holds that one may slaughter [and sprinkle], for it is not reasonable that they would disagree on this; rather, they hold that Rabbi Akiva derives [it] from one impure from a corpse even though it is not so similar to it. And it appears to the Ri that he does not derive "distant journey" from "ritually impure" through a heikesh [scriptural analogy], but rather through a mah matzinu ["just as we find"]; for if [it were] from a heikesh, what is Rav Naḥman answering [by saying] that he holds one may slaughter [and sprinkle]? Even so, let us derive from it, since one cannot refute a heikesh! And it is somewhat difficult for the Ri, for if it is not a heikesh, there are many [objections] to raise.

Tosafot on Pesachim 93a:2:1.hebrew: רבי עקיבא סבר אין שוחטין וזורקין - תימה: מנא ליה? דהא לעיל (פסחים דף צ:) אמר דמ"ד אין שוחטין סבר לה כרבי יצחק, דאמר: טמאי מתים היו שחל כו', וקדריש: "ביום ההוא" אין יכולים לעשות, הא למחר יכולים; ואילו ר"ע בפרק הישן (סוכה ד' כה:) לית ליה דרבי יצחק:
Tosafot on Pesachim 93a:2:1.english: Rabbi Akiva holds [that] one may not slaughter and sprinkle - [This is] surprising: from where does he [derive] this? For earlier (Pesachim 90b) [the Gemara] stated that the one who says one may not slaughter holds in accordance with Rabbi Yitzchak, who said: They were impure from a corpse whose [seventh day] fell, etc., and he expounds [the verse]: "On that day" they are unable to perform [the offering], but on the next day they are able; whereas Rabbi Akiva, in chapter HaYashen (Sukkah 25b), does not hold [the teaching] of Rabbi Yitzchak.

Tosafot on Pesachim 93a:4:1.hebrew: דאי בעי למיעבד לא שבקינן ליה - תימה, הואיל וסבירא ליה להאי תנא שוחטין על טמא שרץ — מדקאמר "לפוטרו מהיכרת", משמע: מכרת פטור, אבל אם זרק הורצה; ומ"ד הורצה, אסיקנא לעיל (פסחים דף פא.) דסבר שוחטין וזורקין — אם כן, טמא דקרא הוא שאינו יכול לאכול בלילה, והיכי קאמר התלמודא דלהכי כתביה: "דאי בעי למיעבד לא שבקינן ליה"? פשיטא דלא שבקינן ליה, כיון דלא חזי למיכל! א] ומ"לפי אכלו" נפקא, דטמא נמי נפק' לן מהתם, כדאמר בפ"ב דזבחים (דף כג.). וי"ל, דודאי קרא לא איצטריך להכי, אלא פריך משום דקתני: "למה נאמר טמא — לפוטרו מהיכרת", דמשמע: מכרת פטור, אבל אי בעי למיעבד מצי עביד; הלכך פריך: הא אי בעי למיעבד לא שבקינן ליה! והשתא טמא לא איצטריך למיכתב אלא לאשמעינן דאיש נדחה ואין ציבור נדחין. ונראה לר"י, דממתניתין דקתני "שאלו פטורין מהיכרת" ליכא למידק כרב נחמן — מדקתני "פטורין", מכלל דאם זרק הורצה — דה"ה אם זרק לא הורצה, ואיידי דקתני סיפא "חייבין" תנא רישא "פטורין". ואתי שפיר, דלעיל מייתי ראיה ממתניתין לרב ששת:
Tosafot on Pesachim 93a:4:1.english: For if he wants to perform [it], we do not allow him - This is astonishing: since this Tanna holds that one may slaughter [the Paschal lamb] on behalf of someone ritually impure from a creeping creature (sheretz) — as he says, "to exempt him from karet," implying that he is exempt from karet, yet if [the priest] sprinkled [the blood], it is accepted; and [regarding] the one who says it is accepted, we concluded above (Pesachim 81a) that he holds one may slaughter and sprinkle [for one impure from a sheretz] — if so, the impure person of the verse [must be one] who cannot eat [the sacrifice] at night! How, then, can the Talmud say that [the Torah] wrote it for this reason: "for if he wants to perform [it], we do not allow him"? It is obvious that we do not allow him, since he is not fit to eat! [a] Furthermore, it is derived from "according to his eating" (lefi ochlo), for [the disqualification of] an impure person is also derived from there, as stated in the second chapter of Zevachim (23a). And one can answer that certainly the verse is not needed for this; rather, [the Gemara] asks because [the baraita] teaches: "Why is 'impure' stated? To exempt him from karet," which implies that he is exempt from karet, yet if he wants to perform [it], he may perform [it]. Therefore, it asks: Surely if he wants to perform [it], we do not allow him! And now, "impure" did not need to be written except to teach us that an individual is deferred [to the second Pesach], whereas a community is not deferred. And it appears to the Ri that from our Mishnah, which teaches "for these are exempt from karet," one cannot infer like Rav Nachman — [namely,] from the fact that it teaches "they are exempt," by implication if [the blood] was sprinkled it is accepted — for the same is true [even] if [the blood] was sprinkled: it is not accepted, and since the latter clause teaches "they are liable," the former clause taught "they are exempt." And [this] fits well, for above [the Gemara] brings a proof from our Mishnah for Rav Sheshet:

Tosafot on Pesachim 93a:4:2.hebrew: אלא למה נאמר דרך רחוקה כו' - קשה לרב יהודה דאמר לקמן: "איזהו דרך רחוקה? כל שאין יכול ליכנס בשעת אכילה" — "דרך רחוקה" דכתב רחמנא למה לי? פשיטא דפטור, דהא לא חזי לאכילה! ואי משום דיכול ליכנס בסוסים ובפרדים — א"כ, לקמן דקתני: "היה חוץ למודיעים ויכול ליכנס בסוסים ובפרדים, יכול יהא חייב? ת"ל: 'ובדרך לא היה'" — ואמאי איצטריך ההוא קרא? הא לא איצטריך למיכתב כלל "דרך רחוקה" אלא משום היכא דיכול ליכנס בסוסים ובפרדים! ואין לומר דס"ד דחייב כרת על מה שהרחיק עצמו, דאם כן מאי פריך "למה נאמר טמא? דאי בעי למיעבד לא שבקינן ליה"? הא שפיר קאמר דנאמר לפוטרו מכרת, דס"ד דליחייב על מה שטימא עצמו! ונראה לרשב"א ד"טמא" ו"דרך רחוקה" איצטריך למיכתב דלא נימא: כיון דלא חזי בראשון לא ליעבד בשני; וסבר כרבי נתן דשני תשלומין דראשון הוא:
Tosafot on Pesachim 93a:4:2.english: "Rather, why is 'a distant journey' stated, etc." - This is difficult according to Rav Yehudah, who says later: "What is 'a distant journey'? Anyone who cannot enter by the time of eating [the Paschal lamb]" — why do I need "a distant journey" that the Merciful One wrote? It is obvious that he is exempt, since he is not fit for eating [it]! And if [you say it is needed] because he can enter on horses and mules — if so, later where it teaches: "[If] he was beyond Modi'im and can enter on horses and mules, one might think he should be liable; Scripture teaches: 'and he was not on a journey'" — why is that verse needed? Surely "a distant journey" did not need to be written at all except for a case where he can enter on horses and mules! And one cannot say that it might have entered your mind that he is liable to karet for having distanced himself, for if so, why does [the Gemara] object: "Why is 'impure' stated? For if he wanted to perform [it], we do not allow him!"? Surely it could well say that it is stated to exempt him from karet, as it might have entered your mind that he would be liable for having rendered himself impure! And it appears to Rashba that "impure" and "a distant journey" needed to be written so that we would not say: since he was not fit [to offer] on the first [Pesaḥ], let him not perform [it] on the second; and [this] holds like Rabbi Natan, that the second [Pesaḥ] is a compensation for the first.

Tosafot on Pesachim 93a:6:1.hebrew: לא קשיא הא ר' יוסי - תימה, דמוקי הך ברייתא דסבר שוחטין וזורקין על טמא שרץ כר' יוסי; ובפ' כיצד צולין (לעיל פסחים דף פא.) גבי טומאת התהום, מסיק דקסבר ר' יוסי אין שוחטין וזורקין כו'. וי"ל דהכא לא מוקי לה כר' יוסי, אלא במאי דסבר דנשים בשני חובה:
Tosafot on Pesachim 93a:6:1.english: "Not difficult: this [is] Rabbi Yosei" - [This is] astonishing, for [the Gemara] establishes this baraita—which holds that one slaughters and sprinkles [the blood] on behalf of one who is impure [due to] a creeping creature—in accordance with Rabbi Yosei; yet in the chapter [entitled] Keitzad Tzolin (above, Pesachim 81a), regarding impurity of the deep, [the Gemara] concludes that Rabbi Yosei holds one does not slaughter and sprinkle, etc. And one can answer that here [the Gemara] does not establish it in accordance with Rabbi Yosei [entirely], but only regarding that which he holds that women on the second [Pesaḥ] are obligated.
